analysis.title: Taiwan's GDP beats forecasts yet again in the third quarter
key_insights: Taiwan's 3Q26 GDP growth accelerated to 14.36% YoY from 12.93% YoY in 2Q26, beating expectations (market 12%, ING 11.4%) despite repeated forecast upgrades.
Domestic demand contributed 9.41ppt to 3Q26 growth versus 4.94ppt from net external demand, even as Taiwan keeps posting record trade surpluses.
Gross capital formation contributed 6.32ppt to growth, up from 4.3ppt in 2Q26, as Taiwanese tech companies expand capacity to meet strong AI-related customer demand.
Private final consumption (2.3ppt) and government final consumption (0.79ppt) were modest contributors compared with capital formation.
Net exports contributed 4.94ppt in 3Q26, the lowest since 1Q25. ING flags that the base effect from last year's surge could cut into growth in coming quarters.
ING raised its full-year GDP forecasts for Taiwan to 13.1% YoY for 2026 and 9.5% YoY for 2027.

sector_views.rationale: Taiwanese tech companies are aggressively expanding capacity to meet strong AI demand, which is driving gross capital formation and GDP growth.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Accelerated from 12.93% YoY in 2Q26 and beat the market consensus of 12% and ING's 11.4%, driven by capex tied to AI demand.

risk_factors: Base effect from last year's surge in net exports could cut into Taiwan's growth in the coming quarters.
